name: Use-Case Closure Certification
sprintRole: Reconstruct a user-facing closure claim into acceptance obligations, try to falsify it, repair exposed gaps, and certify only evidence-backed closure
useWhen: A feature, workflow, deployment, or operator use case is being called done/working/closed and the claim needs adversarial acceptance proof rather than a completion summary.
inspectFirst: The original user-facing request and closure claim; current implementation and entrypoints; acceptance criteria; tests/validators; generated artifacts; known incidents; first-run/repeat-run/failure/upgrade/context variants; integration and runtime evidence.
expectedOutput: A reconstructed closure claim, obligation ledger with PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN/NOT-APPLICABLE states, adversarial falsification attempts, repaired in-scope gaps, rerun proof, and an exact certified proof level or reason closure remains open.
nextStep: Translate the user-facing claim into concrete observable obligations, mark current evidence without treating unknown as pass, attack the weakest obligation, repair any exposed gap, and repeat until the claim survives the bounded falsification pass.
proofGate: Every material obligation implied by the claimed use case is explicit and evidence-linked; UNKNOWN is not PASS; at least one deliberate falsification pass covers practical first-run/repeat/failure/upgrade/context variants; exposed in-scope gaps are repaired and revalidated; and certification states the exact proof level without inflating static or synthetic evidence into live closure.
